The dossier's 41 callers are an xref artefact; the exact-target scan finds only 0x119AF4.

name: Container_ObjectDtor
summary: Base-class destructor of the refcounted object family: installs the base vtable, releases the two heap-owned members at +0x0C and +0x10 through the registered deallocator 0x11C814, then walks the singly linked node list at +0x10 clearing each node's two words, and returns self.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly confirms the whole sequence (`str vtable,[r4]`, `blne 0x11c814` twice, the `ldr r1,[r4,#0x10]!` list walk, `sub r0,r4,#0x10` return), and the callers are the script VM's table/value destructors plus a multiple-inheritance destructor that adjusts its pointer first - so this is a shared base destructor, not a one-off.

name: maybe_Snd_SendIpcStatus
signature: int maybe_Snd_SendIpcStatus(unsigned int* session, unsigned int handle, unsigned int flags, unsigned int* out0, unsigned int* out1)
summary: Status query with header 0x00130042 (command 0x13, one normal and two translated words): stores the handle and flags, sends svc 0x32, and on success writes TLS+0x88 to *out1 and TLS+0x90 to *out0 - note the outputs are swapped relative to the parameter order.
evidence: NEW: the exact-target callers are the Gfx_* command/register writers (0x1136D8, 0x113714, 0x11386C, 0x1198DC, 0x11A50C, 0x11F12C, 0x11F21C), which contradicts the Snd prefix - the same command is used by the graphics command stream. The header literal and the swapped outputs are certain, the service is not, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdList_ResetSlot
summary: Marks a slot free: calls the lock helper 0x12032C, resolves the slot with 0x120368 and stores -1 into the word 0x98 bytes before the returned pointer. 0x120368 itself is `mvn r1,#0; str r1,[r0,#0x1c]; bx lr`, so it takes a pointer and invalidates its +0x1C word.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of 0x120368 shows it takes a pointer in r0 (not an index) and stores -1 at +0x1C, so Ghidra's `func_00120368(index)` call is mis-typed and the -0x98 store is a back-reference into the slot header. No exact caller exists, so the command-list ownership is still inferred from the neighbouring 0x1200xx block.

name: maybe_Os_MainRamRangeFragment
summary: Not a function start: the address lies 0x196 bytes inside 0x123E18 (the main-RAM address translator) and repeats its bounds compare plus the 'base + addr' return. It only appears in the batch because a 0xB5xx halfword matched the Thumb-push scan.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller and no data pointer to this address, confirming it is interior code of 0x123E18. The body also depends on caller registers (unaff_r5, in_CY), which per FACTS.md keeps the confidence at 0.3 or below.

name: maybe_std_UnwindPersonalityRoutine
signature: u32 maybe_std_UnwindPersonalityRoutine(void* state, void* ucb, void* context)
summary: ARM EHABI personality routine: calls the unwind bytecode interpreter 0x1250BC, whose inline opcode words follow the call site, and returns an unwind reason code. The whole 0x125098-0x125738 region is C++ exception support, not game code.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller (the dossier's 80 are an xref artefact), and Ghidra cannot decompile past the inline data (halt_baddata), so the body cannot be re-read. The `push {r4,lr}; bl 0x1250BC; .word 0x806DB6DB` shape with inline unwind opcodes is still the EHABI personality signature, which is why the name is kept.

name: maybe_std_CopyPointerListAndSync
summary: Copies a count-driven array of double-dereferenced pointers (desc[1] holds the array, desc[2] the count) into the caller's buffer; for a count of exactly one it instead clears the first word and issues svc 0x24 (wait for one handle).
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller, and the tail call 0x1169DC has no readable body, so the descriptor layout is still inferred from the offsets. The two-pass unrolled copy and the count==1 svc 0x24 path are readable, which is all the name claims.

name: Video_ConvertSelect_A
summary: Dispatcher of the first conversion family: when the context's two leading pointers differ it runs the plane variant 0x1290A0, otherwise the 16-byte block variant 0x12762C, and then always runs the common 32-byte stage 0x1281E0.
evidence: NEW: the sibling copies of this dispatcher are already confident names - Video_ConvertSelect_B (0x12E594) and Video_ConvertSelect_C (0x13230C) - and the literal pool at 0x12A87C publishes 0x12A81C/0x12A84C together, so the '_A' copy is the same function as its two named twins. The '_A' suffix is the copy index, which is exactly what the family uses.

name: Video_ConvertSelectB_A
summary: Dispatcher of the second conversion family: picks the 8-byte in-place variant 0x126B0C or the three-plane variant 0x129EF4 on the same 'pointers differ' test, then always runs the 32-byte stage 0x126EF4.
evidence: NEW: Video_ConvertSelectB_B (0x12E5C4) and Video_ConvertSelectB_C (0x13233C) are already confident names for the same body, and the literal pool at 0x12A87C holds both dispatcher addresses, so the '_A' copy is confirmed by its named twins rather than by a fresh guess.
